item.title: Ise-ebi: The Spiny Lobster of Ise-Shima — Guide
item.description: Ise-ebi, the Japanese spiny lobster, is the most celebrated seafood of the Ise-Shima coast and a symbol of good fortune, its armoured red form long used as an auspicious New Year decoration. Caught in the rocky waters off Mie from autumn through spring, it is prized for firm, sweet, springy flesh that outshines clawed lobsters, and the region serves it every luxurious way: as translucent sashimi (ise-ebi no o-tsukuri), grilled or steamed in the shell, deep-fried, and simmered into a rich miso soup made from the heads.
